amc8-ajhsme-1991-01.title: Check the last digit
amc8-ajhsme-1991-01.body:
The answer must end in $10-7=3$, and it must be a little more than $1-0.78\approx0.22$ trillion. Only $222{,}222{,}222{,}223$ fits.

**Answer: (B) 222,222,222,223**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-03.title: Powers of ten
amc8-ajhsme-1991-03.body:
$200{,}000=2\times10^5$, so the product is $4\times10^{10}=40{,}000{,}000{,}000$, forty billion.

**Answer: (E) forty billion**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-03.title: Count zeros
amc8-ajhsme-1991-03.body:
$2\times2=4$, and the two numbers have $5+5=10$ zeros: $4$ followed by ten zeros $=40{,}000{,}000{,}000$, which is forty billion.

**Answer: (E) forty billion**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-04.title: Distance from 1000
amc8-ajhsme-1991-04.body:
Each number is $1000$ minus something: $9, 7, 5, 3, 1$. So the sum is $5000-(9+7+5+3+1)=5000-25$, giving $N=25$.

**Answer: (E) 25**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-04.title: Use the average
amc8-ajhsme-1991-04.body:
The five numbers average $995$, so the sum is $5\times995=4975=5000-25$. $N=25$.

**Answer: (E) 25**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-05.title: Count the squares
amc8-ajhsme-1991-05.body:
Every domino covers $2$ squares, so a board that can be covered has an even number of squares. $3\times5=15$ is odd, so it cannot be covered. All the others ($12, 16, 20, 18$ squares) have a side of even length and can be tiled by rows of dominoes.

**Answer: (B) $3\times 5$**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-05.title: Colour argument
amc8-ajhsme-1991-05.body:
Each domino covers one black and one white square. The $3\times5$ board has $8$ squares of one colour and $7$ of the other, so it can't be covered.

**Answer: (B) $3\times 5$**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-06.title: Check each row's smallest
amc8-ajhsme-1991-06.body:
Row minimums: $2, 7, 3, 1, 2$. Is each the largest in its column?
- $2$ (column 5: $2,8,9,1,3$): no.
- $7$ (column 2: $6,7,3,4,2$): yes!
- $3$ (column 2): no. $1$ (column 5): no. $2$ (column 2): no.

The answer is $7$.

**Answer: (C) 7**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-06.title: Check the choices
amc8-ajhsme-1991-06.body:
$1$ is not largest in its column, $6$ is not smallest in its row ($2$ is), $12$ and $15$ are not smallest in their row. $7$ is smallest in row 2 and largest in column 2.

**Answer: (C) 7**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-08.title: Big over small, same sign
amc8-ajhsme-1991-08.body:
A positive quotient needs both numbers with the same sign. Positive pairs: largest is $\frac81=8$. Negative pairs: largest is $\frac{-24}{-2}=12$. So the maximum is $12$.

**Answer: (D) $12$**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-08.title: Why not 24?
amc8-ajhsme-1991-08.body:
$24$ would need $\frac{-24}{-1}$ or $\frac{24}{1}$, but neither $-1$ nor $24$ is in the set. The best is $\frac{-24}{-2}=12$.

**Answer: (D) $12$**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-09.title: Inclusion-exclusion
amc8-ajhsme-1991-09.body:
Multiples of $3$: $\lfloor46/3\rfloor=15$. Multiples of $5$: $9$. Multiples of both (of $15$): $3$, counted twice. Total $15+9-3=21$.

**Answer: (B) 21**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-09.title: List the extra fives
amc8-ajhsme-1991-09.body:
There are $15$ multiples of $3$. The multiples of $5$ that are not multiples of $3$ are $5,10,20,25,35,40$: $6$ more. $15+6=21$.

**Answer: (B) 21**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-10.title: Base times height
amc8-ajhsme-1991-10.body:
$BC$ goes from $(0,2)$ to $(4,2)$, length $4$; opposite side $AD$ also has length $4$, so $A=(-1,0)$. The height between the lines $y=0$ and $y=2$ is $2$. Area $=4\times2=8$.

**Answer: (B) 8**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-10.title: Cut and move
amc8-ajhsme-1991-10.body:
Cut off the triangle with vertices $A$, $(0,0)$, $B$ and slide it to the right to fill the triangle $D$, $(4,0)$, $C$. The parallelogram becomes the $4\times2$ rectangle with corners $(0,0)$ and $(4,2)$: area $8$.

**Answer: (B) 8**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-11.title: The other two add to 10
amc8-ajhsme-1991-11.body:
If $5$ is in the set, the other two numbers are different, not $5$, and add to $10$: $\{1,9\},\{2,8\},\{3,7\},\{4,6\}$. That gives $4$ sets.

**Answer: (B) 4**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-11.title: Magic square view
amc8-ajhsme-1991-11.body:
These are exactly the lines through the center of the $3\times3$ magic square (center $5$): one row, one column and two diagonals, $4$ lines.

**Answer: (B) 4**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-12.title: Averages
amc8-ajhsme-1991-12.body:
The left side is the average of $2,3,4$, which is $3$. The sum on the right is $3\times1991$ (average $1991$), so $\frac{3\times1991}{N}=3$ gives $N=1991$.

**Answer: (D) 1991**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-13.title: Count 2s and 5s
amc8-ajhsme-1991-13.body:
$25^7=5^{14}$ and $8^3=2^9$. Each zero needs a pair $2\times5$. There are only $9$ twos, so $9$ zeros: the product is $5^5\times10^9=3125\times10^9$.

**Answer: (C) 9**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-13.title: Make hundreds
amc8-ajhsme-1991-13.body:
$8^3=512=4^4\times2$, so the product is $(25\times4)^4\times25^3\times2=100^4\times31{,}250$. $100^4$ gives $8$ zeros and $31{,}250$ adds one more: $9$ zeros.

**Answer: (C) 9**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-14.title: 13 points is enough
amc8-ajhsme-1991-14.body:
$13$ points means two wins and one second place. In the two races our student won, anyone else gets at most $3$; in the remaining race at most $5$. So any other student has at most $3+3+5=11<13$.

**Answer: (D) 13**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-14.title: Smaller totals fail
amc8-ajhsme-1991-14.body:
The possible totals are sums of three of $0,1,3,5$; $12$ cannot be made. A total of $11$ (e.g. $5+5+1$) can be tied: another student could finish $3,3,5$. Totals of $10$ or less can be beaten or tied too (if you didn't win twice, someone else can win twice). So the smallest guaranteed total is $13$.

**Answer: (D) 13**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-15.title: Track faces
amc8-ajhsme-1991-15.body:
The notch goes all the way across the top of the $1$-foot-wide solid. Cutting it out removes $1$ sq ft from the top, $1$ from the front and $1$ from the back ($3$ removed), and creates the floor of the notch and its two walls ($3$ added). The surface area is the same.

**Answer: (C) the same**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-15.title: Compute both areas
amc8-ajhsme-1991-15.body:
Original: $2(1\cdot3+1\cdot9+3\cdot9)=2(3+9+27)=78$ sq ft.

New: top $9-1=8$, notch floor $1$, two notch walls $1+1$, front and back $27-1=26$ each, two ends $3$ each, bottom $9$: $8+1+2+52+6+9=78$ sq ft. The same.

**Answer: (C) the same**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-16.title: Follow the stacks
amc8-ajhsme-1991-16.body:
Write each stack from top to bottom (by rows).
- After (1): row 1 lies on row 4, row 2 lies on row 3.
- After (2): the lower stack (row 1 on row 4) flips onto the upper one, so each column's stack is: row 4, row 1, row 2, row 3. The bottom is row 3: squares $9,10,11,12$.
- After (3): the right stacks flip onto the left, so the top squares are now the old bottoms of columns 4 and 3: $12$ (left position) and $11$ (right position).
- After (4): the left stack flips onto the right; its old bottom comes on top. The left stack is column 1 with column 4 flipped onto it, and its bottom is row 3, column 1: square $9$.

**Answer: (B) 9**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-16.title: Watch the bottom layer
amc8-ajhsme-1991-16.body:
When a half is folded over, it lands upside down, so its bottom layer becomes the new top. So after step (4) the top square is the bottom layer of the left half just before step (4).

The bottom layer never changes except where paper stays put: after (1) the bottom layer of the remaining strip is row 3 (row 2 was folded onto it), (2) and (3) only add paper on top, so the bottom layer is still row 3, columns 1 and 2: squares $9$ (left) and $10$ (right). Step (4) flips the left stack over, putting $9$ on top.

**Answer: (B) 9**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-17.title: Every other seat
amc8-ajhsme-1991-17.body:
A row with $n$ seats holds at most $\lceil n/2\rceil$ students (seats $1,3,5,\dots$). Rows have $10,11,\dots,29$ seats, giving $5,6,6,7,7,\dots,14,14,15$.

Pair rows $(10,11),(12,13),\dots,(28,29)$: each pair holds $11,13,\dots,29$. The $10$ pair-sums average $20$, total $200$.

**Answer: (C) 200**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-17.title: Count directly
amc8-ajhsme-1991-17.body:
Rows with an even number $2k$ of seats ($k=5,\dots,14$) hold $k$; rows with $2k+1$ seats hold $k+1$. Sum $=(5+\cdots+14)+(6+\cdots+15)=95+105=200$.

**Answer: (C) 200**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-18.title: Count the X's
amc8-ajhsme-1991-18.body:
Each X stands for the same number of employees. Counts by years $1$ to $10$: $5,5,8,3,2,2,2,1,1,1$, total $30$. Five years or more: $2+2+2+1+1+1=9$. $\frac{9}{30}=30\%$.

**Answer: (C) $30\%$**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-18.title: Count the rest
amc8-ajhsme-1991-18.body:
Under $5$ years: $5+5+8+3=21$ of $30$, which is $70\%$. So $100\%-70\%=30\%$ worked $5$ years or more.

**Answer: (C) $30\%$**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-19.title: Make the others small
amc8-ajhsme-1991-19.body:
The sum is $10\times10=100$. To make one number large, make the other nine as small as possible: $1+2+\cdots+9=45$. The largest is then $100-45=55$.

**Answer: (C) 55**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-19.title: Check
amc8-ajhsme-1991-19.body:
$1,2,\dots,9,55$ are different positive whole numbers with sum $100$ and mean $10$. Any other nine different positive numbers have sum at least $45$, so no number can exceed $55$.

**Answer: (C) 55**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-20.title: Write it as an equation
amc8-ajhsme-1991-20.body:
$ABC+AB+A=300$ means $111A+11B+C=300$. If $A=1$, $11B+C=189$, impossible for digits. If $A=2$, $11B+C=78$, so $B=7$, $C=1$ (all different ✓). $A\ge3$ is too big. So $C=1$.

**Answer: (A) 1**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-21.title: Count the steps
amc8-ajhsme-1991-21.body:
From $20^\circ$ to $32^\circ$ is $12^\circ$, which is $4$ steps of $3^\circ$. The volume grew by $4\times4=16$ cm³, so at $20^\circ$ it was $24-16=8$ cm³.

**Answer: (A) 8**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-21.title: Rate
amc8-ajhsme-1991-21.body:
The volume changes by $\frac43$ cm³ per degree. Over $12$ degrees: $12\times\frac43=16$. $24-16=8$.

**Answer: (A) 8**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-22.title: Complement
amc8-ajhsme-1991-22.body:
The product is odd only if both results are odd. First spinner ($1,2,3$): odd with probability $\frac23$. Second ($4,5,6$): odd with probability $\frac13$. $P(\text{odd})=\frac23\cdot\frac13=\frac29$, so $P(\text{even})=1-\frac29=\frac79$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{7}{9}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-22.title: List all 9 outcomes
amc8-ajhsme-1991-22.body:
Odd products: $1\cdot5$ and $3\cdot5$ only. The other $7$ of the $9$ equally likely pairs give even products: $\frac79$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{7}{9}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-23.title: Females first
amc8-ajhsme-1991-23.body:
Females in band or orchestra: $100+80-60=120$. So there are $230-120=110$ males in total. Males in both: $80+100-110=70$. Males in band only: $80-70=10$.

**Answer: (A) 10**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-23.title: Total overlap
amc8-ajhsme-1991-23.body:
Band + orchestra $=180+180=360$ memberships for $230$ students, so $130$ students are in both. Of those, $60$ are female, so $70$ are male. Band males not in orchestra: $80-70=10$.

**Answer: (A) 10**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-24.title: Only one big cube fits
amc8-ajhsme-1991-24.body:
Smaller cubes have edge $1$ or $2$ (not $3$). Two $2$-cubes don't fit in a $3$-cube (they'd overlap in the middle), and not all the same size means at least one $2$-cube. So there is one $2$-cube (volume $8$) and $27-8=19$ unit cubes: $N=20$.

**Answer: (E) 20**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-24.title: Volume check
amc8-ajhsme-1991-24.body:
Volumes: $27=8a+b$ with $a$ cubes of edge $2$ and $b$ of edge $1$. Only $a=1$ is possible geometrically, giving $b=19$ and $N=1+19=20$.

**Answer: (E) 20**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-25.title: Multiply by three fourths
amc8-ajhsme-1991-25.body:
Each change keeps $\frac34$ of every black triangle black. After five changes the black part is $\left(\frac34\right)^5=\frac{243}{1024}$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{243}{1024}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1991-25.title: Count triangles
amc8-ajhsme-1991-25.body:
After each change every black triangle becomes $3$ black triangles, each $\frac14$ the size. After $5$ changes: $3^5=243$ black triangles, each $\frac1{4^5}=\frac1{1024}$ of the original. Black part $\frac{243}{1024}$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{243}{1024}$**
